subject: Renewal + Competitive Bake-off: FastRetail capacity & terms
messages:
From: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@fastretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal timing + upcoming bake-off

Hi Marissa,

Hope you’re well. Quick heads up — our procurement team is planning a formal renewal evaluation for our inference stack (contract up 2/28/26). We’ve been running Redwood in prod for the last 9 months and the platform has generally met our latency needs. That said, the team has initiated a limited bake-off with CloudAI who are pitching a lower unit cost for embeddings and a turnkey ded-CPU option for peak traffic.

A few asks from our side:
- Can you share an updated renewal proposal (12mo and 24mo) with tiered committed capacity pricing?
- Any plan you can offer to mitigate the procurement price comparison (discounts, committed-cap credits, or dedicated reservation pricing)?
- We’ll also need a short summary of recent perf numbers for our peak workloads ahead of the bake-off.

Procurement is cc’d. Timeline: bake-off starts 1/5/26; final decision expected by mid-Jan.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Gomez
Head of ML Platforms, FastRetail
elena.gomez@fastretail.com
+1 415-555-0176

--
Attachment: none

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@fastretail.com>
Cc: procurement@fastretail.com
Date: Fri, 21 Nov 2025 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + upcoming bake-off

Elena — thanks for the heads-up. We definitely want to make this renewal straightforward and keep FastRetail on Redwood. I’m attaching a draft Save Plan that outlines: committed capacity tiers (w/ stepped discounts), a short-term dedicated capacity add-on for peak windows, and a proposal for a bake-off support package (priority eng backing + custom perf tests).

High level offers in the draft:
- 12mo: standard pricing + 10% committed capacity credit at 1.2x current spend
- 24mo: 15% committed credit, option to convert to Dedicated at a capped rate
- Bake-off support: 2 weeks of priority perf engineering to mirror your peak traffic (no extra charge with 24mo)

I can set a quick sync with our perf team and your platform folks next week to scope the tests. Would Tuesday 11/25 at 10am PT work?

Attaching: redwood_save_plan_v2.pdf

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

--
Attachment: redwood_save_plan_v2.pdf

From: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@fastretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, procurement@fastretail.com
Date: Tue, 02 Dec 2025 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + upcoming bake-off

Marissa — thanks for the plan. We ran an initial pass of the bake-off tests this week; results attached. Short summary: Redwood is consistently better on 95th/99th latency for our sessionized workloads, and the model outputs are equivalent. Pricing-wise CloudAI is quoting ~18% lower per-embedding unit if we move to their managed endpoint + reserved capacity. Procurement is pushing that delta hard.

We have a kickoff with procurement and the ML infra team on 12/08 to decide if more negotiation is warranted. Two asks:
1) Can your team run a targeted perf test with KV cache patterns enabled (we think our traffic benefits a lot from prefix caching)?
2) Can you provide a committed-capacity counter-offer that closes the ~18% price gap (or explain what Redwood can offer on value beyond raw per-unit cost)?

Attach: fastretail_bakeoff_results_20251202.csv

Thanks,
Elena

--
Attachment: fastretail_bakeoff_results_20251202.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Dec 2025 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Renewal timing + upcoming bake-off (FastRetail)

Team — forwarding FastRetail's bake-off output. Procurement is leaning toward CloudAI on price; FastRetail values our latency and advanced features (prefix/KV cache) but the ~18% gap is topical. We need a retention/save plan that is defensible to procurement and quick to sign.

What I need by EOD Monday 12/08:
- Rishi: commercial play (price delta to close; recommended committed tiers + timeline)
- Priyom: a scoped perf test plan to validate cache-enabled throughput and expected cost reductions (2–3 test scenarios + estimated run time)
- Steph: approval thresholds for concessioning (how much discount can we offer before this needs director sign-off)
- Olga: legal note on term changes we can make in a short turnaround (SLA/credits, dedicated options)

We should aim to keep this within a 10–12% net-cost delta via a combination of commit + dedicated credits + bake-off support. I’ll coordinate a call with Elena for 12/08.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Internal only

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2025 16:30:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Fwd: Renewal timing + upcoming bake-off (FastRetail)

Marissa / team — draft perf plan below. I’ll own running the tests with our perf lab and provide a short deliverable for FastRetail's ML infra folks.

Planned tests (targeting 12/08 window):
1) KV prefix caching simulation (their sessionized pattern): 1M requests, measured 95/99 latencies, per-token cost delta with/without caching. ~6 hours run time.
2) Dedicated pool emulation: allocate a 2x dedicated instance for a 3-hour peak window; measure tail latency and tokens/sec. ~3 hours run time.
3) Cost-projection matrix: run smaller-scale sampling to estimate per-embedding and per-token unit cost under committed tiers.

Concessions we can offer to close the gap:
- 12mo commitment at 1.2x current spend -> 12% effective discount via committed credits + 5% sign-up credit for dedicated-window usage.
- 24mo at 1.5x -> 18% effective discount + free bake-off perf support (2 weeks).
- Short-term: offer a Temp Price Match window (45 days) for the first 3 months if they commit to a 12mo with a 60% commit share on embeddings.

Technical risks / notes:
- We can replicate their traffic patterns in our lab; KV caching should show a meaningful cost/latency win but we need their exact prefix distribution.
- Dedicated pool pricing needs legal sign-off if we cap rates below published Dedicated pricing.

I’ll prep the perf report and a short exec summary for the 12/08 call.

— Priyom
Senior Perf Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@fastretail.com>, procurement@fastretail.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Jan 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood save plan + perf report follow-up (FastRetail)

Elena / team — thanks for the call this morning. Attached is the perf summary from Priyom (KV caching + dedicated emulation) and an updated Save Plan that reflects the concessions we discussed. Highlights:
- 12mo offer: 12% effective discount via committed credits at 1.2x current spend + 5% dedicated-window credit for the first 3 months.
- 24mo offer: 18% effective discount, includes 2 weeks of bake-off engineering and 1 emergency-fallback pool for Black Friday traffic at capped rates.
- Performance: KV caching cut 95th latency by ~22% in our simulation and reduced estimated per-token spend by ~14% at their traffic profile. See perf CSV.

We’re also willing to provide a 45-day temporary price match on base embedding units for a 12mo commitment, refundable if FastRetail downgrades within the first 60 days.

Next steps: I’ve attached the term sheet and a DocuSign link for the 12mo option with the temp price match. If procurement is ready, we can sign and onboard the dedicated windows by 1/20.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/link/FASTR-8721-sign
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234568/deal/8721

Attachments: fastretail_bakeoff_results_20251202.csv, final_term_sheet_fastretail_20260115.pdf

Best,
Marissa

From: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@fastretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, procurement@fastretail.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 17:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood save plan + perf report follow-up (FastRetail)

Marissa — appreciate the extra legwork and the KV results. Procurement reviewed the final term sheet and accepted the 12mo offer with the 45-day temp price match. We’ve completed signature on the DocuSign link.

Two asks for the first 30 days post-sign:
- A kickoff with your Dedicated ops lead to schedule the first emergency-fallback pool for peak testing.
- An exec one-pager summarizing backup/fallback policies and response SLAs for our legal team.

We’re happy to continue with Redwood — thanks for moving quickly.

— Elena
